conventions.convention: Complex L2 consists of almost-everywhere classes; its inner product is integral f conjugate(g), linear in the first argument. Weak-derivative tests are bilinear, without conjugation.
Q_j is multiplication by x_j on {f: x_j f ∈ L2}; P_j = −iℏ D_j on {f: D_j f ∈ L2}. In dimensions greater than one, D(P_j) need not equal W1,2.
The Fourier kernel is exp(−2πi x·ξ); momentum has multiplier 2πℏ ξ_j. Translation T_a f(x) = f(x−a) gives T_a Q_j T_a inverse = Q_j−a_j.
Magnetic data are real bounded classes A_j with all weak first derivatives bounded, and a real bounded scalar class Φ. ℏ,m > 0, q ∈ R, the spatial dimension is three, and D(K_A,Φ) = W2,2.
G(t) multiplies by exp(iqχ/ℏ); χ has uniformly bounded first and second spatial derivatives and bounded time derivative. The transported potentials are A′ = A + ∇χ and Φ′ = Φ − ∂tχ.

Coherent normalization requires a+b ≠ 0; mixed normalization requires both amplitudes nonzero. Marker weights are normalized only when Ψ ≠ 0. Frequency moments are conditional on N ≥ 1 independent trials with the specified common success probability.
The Ehrenfest timescale is ΔA/|f′| only at points where f′ ≠ 0, for a normalized graph-domain differentiable solution. It is not a time observable or apparatus-error quantity.

The spin basis is ordered (e_1/2,e_−1/2), S_z has diagonal entries ±ℏ/2, B_z and B_z′ are bounded, and the force identity uses initial data in D(K²). The constant-gradient simplification is asserted only at preparation time.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and Countable Choice, for d ≥ 1 and ℏ > 0, Q_j and P_j are self-adjoint on their maximal domains; D(P_j) = {f: ξ_j F2 f ∈ L2} and F2(P_j f) = 2πℏ ξ_j F2 f. Translations are unitary, preserve the stated domains and W1,2 and W2,2, commute with momentum, and conjugate Q_j to Q_j−a_j.
Under Countable Choice, if a and all its weak first derivatives are bounded classes on R^d and u ∈ W1,2, then au ∈ W1,2 and D_j(au) = a D_j u + (D_j a)u as L2 classes. No boundedness of u is assumed.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for ℏ,m > 0, real q and admissible (A,Φ), P_A,j is self-adjoint on D(P_j), the stated magnetic-square expansion holds on W2,2, and K_A,Φ is symmetric and self-adjoint on W2,2. For every a ∈ (0,1), a finite b ≥ 0 gives ||(K_A,Φ−K0)u|| ≤ a||K0u||+b||u||; consequently K_A,Φ is bounded below.

Under its stated AC, coefficient and gauge-regularity hypotheses, G(t) is unitary, maps W1,2 and W2,2 onto themselves, satisfies (P_j−q(A_j+D_jχ))G(t)u = G(t)(P_j−qA_j)u for u ∈ W1,2, and is strongly continuous and strongly differentiable on each fixed L2 vector with derivative (iq/ℏ)(∂tχ)G(t).

Under Countable Choice, symmetric densely defined A,B and unit u ∈ D(A)∩D(B) satisfy (ΔA)²(ΔB)² ≥ Cov_u(A,B)² + (Im⟨x,y⟩)², with equality exactly when the centered vectors are linearly dependent. On D(AB)∩D(BA), ⟨[A,B]u,u⟩ = −2i Im⟨x,y⟩.

Under AC and Countable Choice on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, bounded operators commuting with every spectral projection of K commute with U(t); a bounded self-adjoint S satisfying SK ⊆ KS also commutes with U(t). Commuting PVM laws are conserved for density operators and unit vectors, energy moments k=1,2 are conserved for unit ψ ∈ D(K), and unit eigenvectors evolve by their scalar phase.

Under Countable Choice, self-adjoint K,A and the stated graph-C1 solution hypotheses with Kψ ∈ D(A) give f′ = −(2/ℏ)Im⟨Aψ,Kψ⟩; the commutator expression additionally requires Aψ ∈ D(K). For normalized ψ and f′(t0) ≠ 0, ΔK(t0)τ_A(t0) ≥ ℏ/2.

Under Countable Choice on a sigma-finite measure space, the specified nonzero coherent and mixed amplitudes define normalized bin measures. The signed difference and normalized marker-weight formulas hold with their stated nonzero denominators; independent N-trial bin frequencies have mean p and variance p(1−p)/N.

concerns.concern: Steps 1.3–1.4 use b_j and the operator P-tilde_j before either is defined; their definitions occur only in step 2.1. The argument is recoverable, but supplier-before-use proof order is broken.

Step 1.5 proves translation commutation with weak derivatives for f ∈ W1,2. Step 2.2 applies that step to arbitrary h ∈ D(P_j), which is larger than W1,2 when d > 1. The same test-function calculation works assuming only D_j h ∈ L2, but that extension is not stated.

F8 says the cited χ_R is 'χ_R=1 on [−R,R]^3'. The supplier lem-schwartz-cutoffs-from-the-standard-smooth-step states ball regions and constructs χ(x)=σ((4−|x|²)/3). At x=(R,R,R), its χ_R equals σ(1/3), strictly less than one. Thus this fact is false for the explicitly cited construction. The limiting proof needs only the actual ball cutoff properties, but the incorrect fact requires correction.

F5 writes w(x)=integral F2w(ξ) exp(2πix·ξ)dξ to establish W2,2 ⊆ L∞. The cited Plancherel statement supplies a unitary extension, not this pointwise inverse-integral representation. A short justification using integrability of F2w and L2 inversion is needed; thm-l-two-fourier-inversion was opened and supplies the relevant inverse-transform limit. The three-dimensional weighted Cauchy–Schwarz estimate is otherwise sound.

alerts.finding: The page summary says the matrices 'J_z e_m = m e_m and J_± e_m = ... on C^{2s+1} are self-adjoint'. The cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices clause (a) instead states J_+* = J_− and self-adjointness of J_z,J_x,J_y. For s=1/2, J_+ is the nonzero upper triangular matrix with only its upper-right entry equal to one, so it is not self-adjoint. The proposition itself states the correct result.
